name: An impossible two-slot triangle
why: Every scope has two full local supports. Repeating local GAC removes nothing, yet no assignment satisfies all three scopes together.

name: A satisfiable triangle still hides pruning
why: Only x2=v2 has joint support. Each binary scope separately supports x2=v0 and x2=v1, so the local fixed point misses them.

name: One global triangle scope
why: Same distinctness solution set as three binary scopes, stronger single-scope propagation. Both variants run their full fixed-point procedure.

name: Propagation crosses scopes
why: x0 forces x1, then x1 forces x2, then x2 forces x3. Synchronous rounds show every update rather than hiding the worklist.

name: Unscoped variables may repeat values
why: Only x0 and x1 must differ. x2 may equal either. The whole tuple is not one global all-different constraint.

name: An unrelated empty domain
why: The nonempty scope has local supports, but the unscoped empty domain still prevents any full assignment. Local-consistent verdict includes all domains.

name: No scopes
why: Every Cartesian tuple is allowed, including repeated values. Local propagation changes nothing.

name: Empty scope and empty tuple
why: The empty all-different constraint and empty assignment both hold. One joint solution, no edges.

name: Maximum Cartesian family
why: Six variables and eight values, no scopes: 262144 full assignments. This is a tiny enumeration cap, not a scalability result.
